why: THE ONLY MUTATION OF THIS PAIR WITH TEETH, which is why it replaced two rows that each claimed to be a survivor. The tail of qualityBars is `if fullBar < demotionBar { fullBar = demotionBar }` followed by `if fullBar < 1 { fullBar = 1 }`, and demotionBar has already been floored to 1 above. So the ordering clamp can only fire when fullBar would be 0, and in that case demotionBar is EXACTLY 1 (it was clamped to the same votable/3, then floored) - both clamps therefore yield fullBar == 1 and deleting either one ALONE cannot change the program. Those two single deletions sat in KNOWN-GAPS as 'the full bar may be zero' and 'the ladder may invert'; both were invalid mutations and both stated consequences were false. MEASURED, full kourtv2 suite each time: ordering clamp alone PASS, unit floor alone PASS, BOTH deleted FAIL at TestTheQualityBarsNeverReachZeroOnAMicroCourt with 'the full bar is 0; an EMPTY tally clears a bar of zero', control green before and after. The lines are adjacent and each occurs once, so the joint deletion is writable as one row - a masking pair does not always mean no row can be written. What it costs if it goes: applyQualityTally opens with `turnout >= fullBar && cs.qHighW*3 >= turnout*2`, which at fullBar == 0 and an empty tally reads 0 >= 0 && 0 >= 0, so a vote nobody cast CONCLUSIVELY promotes the claim to the high-quality payout multiplier.

label: Cost: the int64 ceiling is off by one
why: PROMOTED FROM KNOWN-GAPS: the row invited construction ('IF SOMEONE CONSTRUCTS the exact case, promote it') and the case exists. Its own argument was incomplete, not wrong about the difficulty: it searched d = 1, said the numerator must be 2^64-2 whose factor pairs have opposite parity, and stopped. The window is ((q-1)m, qm], so at d = 1 the numerator may also be 2^64-3 - odd, factoring as 1 x (2^64-3), same parity, integral from and s1. That one dies on the CAP (New refuses cap > 2^50, and it needs s1 = 2^63-1), which is the real obstruction and not parity. Searching under the cap: diff = k*Q with Q = 2^63-1 = 7^2 * 73 * 127 * 337 * 92737 * 649657 makes m = k exactly, so any even k whose k*Q factors as (s1-from)(s1+from) with s1 <= 2^50 lands the quotient ON the ceiling. 74 solutions; the first is d=2, from=994862694074946, delta=18542, where q = 9223372036854775807 exactly, guard 1 (hi2 >= m) does not fire because hi2 = 1 < m = 4, and Cost returns (MaxInt64, true) intact against (0, false) mutated.
